properties.statement: THE INSTALLER HAS A GUARD FOR 'IGNORING A TRACKED FILE DOES NOTHING' AND IT STRUCTURALLY CANNOT FIRE FOR `.reflow2/` — THE ONE ENTRY MOST LIKELY TO BE ALREADY TRACKED. Reported 2026-08-08 by Alex, an early adopter who started on v0.0.5: his `.gitignore` contains `.reflow2` and git is nonetheless tracking `.reflow2/graph/LOG`, `.reflow2/graph/fulltext/meta.json` and `.reflow2/graph/fulltext/.managed.json`. His question was whether the installer or his agent had written the ignore line, and what he is supposed to be committing at all. BOTH HALVES ARE THE INSTALLER'S. `tools/reflow2_init.py ensure_gitignore()` writes the block, and `IGNORE_LINES` carries `.reflow2/` — so the ignore line is ours, not his agent's. The same function then loops the ignore lines to warn about any git is ALREADY tracking, because `already_tracked`'s own docstring says it plainly: 'gitignore does not untrack a tracked file, so saying "ignored" without saying that would be a half-truth.' THE LOOP OPENS `if line.endswith("/"): continue`. `.reflow2/` is the ONLY entry ending in a slash, so the warning is skipped for exactly the path it matters most for — and it matters most there because the store is created the moment you first use reflow2, long before anyone runs the installer that would ignore it, so `git add .` in between tracks it forever. MEASURED, NOT REASONED, AND IT CORRECTED MY OWN HYPOTHESIS. I assumed the check would also fail on a directory path and that the skip was therefore a workaround. Reproduced in a scratch repo — commit two files under `.reflow2/`, add the ignore rule afterwards — and `git ls-files --error-unmatch '.reflow2/'` returns 0, correctly reporting the directory as tracked. SO THE UNDERLYING CHECK WORKS AND THE SKIP IS THE WHOLE BUG. FIX SHAPE: drop the `endswith('/')` skip; the existing `already_tracked` call is correct for a directory as written. Optionally report the count and the remedy per path — `git ls-files -- '.reflow2/'` names the tracked files, and `git rm -r --cached .reflow2` is the fix a user needs to be told. WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN ITS SIZE: this is a silent wrong answer to a user who did everything right. Alex read his .gitignore, saw `.reflow2`, and reasonably concluded the graph was excluded. The installer ran, said nothing, and the store stayed in version control — which is the class of failure req:no-silent-fallback exists for, in the one tool a new user meets first. A SECOND, UNTESTED RISK WORTH STATING AS UNTESTED: a committed `fulltext/meta.json` is tantivy index metadata, so checking out an older commit would restore a stale index descriptor over live segment files. I did not test whether that corrupts the index or is merely ignored; `.reflow2/graph/LOG` is RocksDB's info log and is only noise.
